chapters.title: Endurance, wisdom, and doing the word

parts.text: James addresses the twelve tribes scattered abroad. He calls them to rejoice in trials because tested faith produces patience, and to ask God for wisdom without wavering. Wealth passes like a flower, while those who endure temptation receive the promised crown of life. God does not entice anyone to evil: desire gives birth to sin and death. Every good gift comes from the unchanging Father, who brings his people forth through the word of truth.

They must listen readily, restrain speech and anger, and receive the word meekly. Hearing without doing is self-deception. Genuine religion includes a bridled tongue, care for orphans and widows, and remaining unspotted by the world.

chapters.title: No partiality, and no lifeless faith

parts.text: James condemns favoring wealthy visitors over the poor. Such partiality contradicts faith in the Lord of glory and the royal law of loving one’s neighbor. Breaking one command makes a person a transgressor of the law. Speech and conduct should reflect coming judgment under the law of liberty; those who show no mercy face judgment without mercy.

He then challenges a claim to faith that does nothing for a needy brother or sister. Faith without works is dead, and belief that there is one God is also shared by devils. Abraham’s offering of Isaac and Rahab’s reception of the messengers illustrate faith acting with works. James concludes that justification is not by faith only: faith without works is as dead as a body without its spirit.

chapters.title: The tongue and the wisdom from above

parts.text: James warns against many becoming teachers because of stricter judgment. Everyone stumbles, and control of speech reflects control of the whole person. Though small, the tongue directs and destroys like a rudder or a spreading fire. No man can tame its unruly evil. Using the same mouth to bless God and curse people made in his likeness is a contradiction that should not occur.

True wisdom should appear in good conduct and meekness. Bitter envy and strife produce confusion and evil, revealing earthly, sensual, devilish wisdom. Wisdom from above is pure, peaceable, gentle, receptive, merciful, fruitful, impartial, and sincere. Peacemakers sow the fruit of righteousness in peace.

chapters.title: Submit to God and abandon proud boasting

parts.text: Quarrels arise from desires warring within people. They lack because they do not ask, or ask with selfish motives. Friendship with the world is enmity with God, who resists the proud and gives grace to the humble. James calls for submission to God, resistance to the devil, cleansed hands and hearts, repentance, and humility before the Lord.

Believers must not slander or presume to judge one another, for God alone is the lawgiver able to save and destroy. Plans for future trade and profit must acknowledge that life is brief and depends on the Lord’s will. Boastful confidence is evil, and knowing the good without doing it is sin.

James warns wealthy oppressors that hoarded riches, withheld wages, luxury, and the killing of the just will testify against them. The laborers’ cries reach the Lord. The brethren must wait patiently for his coming, like a farmer awaiting rain, and refrain from grudging against one another. The prophets and Job exemplify endurance, while God’s compassion provides encouragement. Their speech should be plain and truthful without oaths.

The afflicted should pray, the joyful sing, and the sick call the elders for prayer and anointing. James joins confession, prayer, healing, and forgiveness, citing Elias’s effective prayers concerning rain. He closes by urging the restoration of those who wander from the truth, which saves a soul from death and covers many sins.
